newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NUTRICIA DISMISSES BABY MILK CLAIMS.
newsitem.headline: NUTRICIA DISMISSES BABY MILK CLAIMS.

text.p: Dutch foods group Nutricia on Thursday dismissed claims that it flouted international codes protecting infant health.

Research by the Interagency Group on Breastfeeding Monitoring (IGBM) earlier showed that several firms were violating the World Health Organisation's (WHO) International Code of Marketing Breast Milk Substitutes.
"We fully respect the international codes," a Nutricia spokesman told the Dutch ANP news agency.
"Our labels clearly state that breast feeding is best. But there has to be an alternative for when a mother can't or won't breast feed."
The spokesman said that, while the WHO code referred to feeding guidelines for babies up to six months, the survey dealt with feeding up to 24 months.
Nutricia is market leader in baby milk substitutes in Poland, one of four countries studied by the IGBM report.
